en: The Pasig River occasionally flows backward during high tide because the rising sea level in Manila Bay becomes higher than the river's water level.
Mayon Volcano has a perfect conical shape because its highly viscous lava cools quickly and piles up near the vent instead of flowing far away.
Lake Taal occupies a large crater because a massive ancient volcanic eruption emptied the underground magma chamber, causing the ground above it to collapse and fill with rain.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the underground limestone rock over millions of years, carving out the massive cave system.
The Sierra Madre mountain range shields eastern Luzon from severe typhoon damage because its dense, towering forests act as a physical windbreak that slows down storm winds.
Maria Cristina Falls generates massive amounts of hydroelectric power because the Agus River drops rapidly from Lake Lanao, using gravity to spin the facility's electricity-producing turbines.
The southwest monsoon brings heavy rainfall to the western Philippines because the prevailing winds pick up massive amounts of moisture from the warm South China Sea before hitting land.
The Philippine archipelago exists because the Eurasian and Philippine Sea tectonic plates continuously collide, pushing the ocean floor upward to form volcanic islands and mountain ranges.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent severe soil erosion because their stepped stone walls slow down rainwater runoff, allowing the soil to absorb the water instead of washing away.
The Tiwi geothermal power plant produces clean electricity because underground magma heats trapped rainwater into steam, which is piped to the surface to spin electrical turbines.
The Verde Island Passage supports immense marine biodiversity because its strong ocean currents mix nutrient-rich waters from two different seas, providing abundant food for thriving coral reefs.
Tubbataha Reef remains pristine because its isolated location in the middle of the Sulu Sea protects the fragile corals from destructive coastal pollution and human fishing activities.
